message.reasoning_content: No new tasks. The description model exists; I can add a small refinement useful to claims c1/c2: an important observation—the matrix is (orthogonal * upper * orthogonal.T)/... with /4 scaling — note orthogonal is scaled by 1/4, and the similarity transform left = orthogonal @ upper, matrix = left @ orthogonal.T. Since orthogonal/4 rows are orthonormal (each row norm 1/4*sqrt(16)=1... actually entries ±0.25, 16 entries → norm 1). So it's a genuine orthogonal similarity, spectral radius up to 0.96875. Also fp16 mantissa 10 bits: values ~0.1, ulp ~6e-5. 64 steps, per-step relative ~5e-4? Actually fp16 relative rounding ~2^-11≈4.9e-4, sqrt(64)*that ≈ 3.9e-3 > 0.002 if errors behave like random walk relative to norm ~0.1... but relative errors vs state norm: absolute error per step ~0.1*4.9e-4≈5e-5; sum ~64*5e-5=3e-3 could exceed 0.002*||ref|| (~0.1 norm → error budget ~2e-3... borderline). Record a refinement update noting the workload favors c1 being borderline: geometric decay of initial contribution plus random drive keeps state ~O(0.1) (stationary std ~0.1/sqrt(1-rho^2)~0.26). Also note dyadic matrix values multiply exactly in fp16 products? Products of dyadic fp16-representable values are fp16 representable when in range... actually 0.875 etc. are dyadic, but fp32 sums still round. Fine — record update.
